articles.title: QualificaDF abre 10 mil vagas para cursos gratuitos no DF; veja como se inscrever | G1
articles.standfirst: Há oportunidades para assistente administrativo, cuidador de idosos, cabeleireiro, eletricista, manutenção de celulares e outras áreas. Inscrições vão até sexta-feira (6)
articles.summary: Há oportunidades para assistente administrativo, cuidador de idosos, cabeleireiro, eletricista, manutenção de celulares e outras áreas. Inscrições vão até sexta-feira (6)
articles.body:
QualificaDF abre 10 mil vagas para cursos gratuitos no DF — Foto: Sejus/divulgação

O QualificaDF está com 10 mil vagas abertas para cursos gratuitos de qualificação profissional no Distrito Federal.

As inscrições podem ser feitas pela internet até sexta-feira (6), por meio do portal da Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Econômico, Trabalho e Renda (Sedet-DF).

Para participar, o candidato deve, em regra, ter pelo menos 18 anos, morar no DF e possuir a escolaridade mínima exigida para o curso escolhido.

Caso sobrem vagas, jovens de 16 a 18 anos também poderão participar, mediante autorização dos responsáveis.

As aulas serão realizadas em unidades de ensino em Ceilândia, Santa Maria, Paranoá e Plano Piloto, nos turnos matutino, vespertino e noturno. Os cursos têm 240 horas de duração, distribuídas em 20 horas semanais.

O edital ainda reserva 10% das vagas para pessoas com deficiência (PcDs).

Resultado e primeira chamada: prevista para 9 de novembro;

Confirmação da matrícula: de 9 a 12 de novembro;

Segunda chamada, se houver vagas: a partir de 13 de novembro;

Início previsto das aulas: 23 de novembro.

Os selecionados terão direito a kit educacional, duas camisetas de uniforme, Passe Livre Estudantil durante o curso, lanche diário e seguro contra acidentes pessoais.

Para receber o certificado, é necessário atingir pelo menos 75% de aproveitamento do conteúdo e 80% de frequência.

articles.summary: O aulão de redação Enem DF da Defensoria Pública acontece nesta quinta na CLDF com dicas para a redação Enem 2026 e análise de temas sociais e ambientais.
articles.body:
Cadernos de prova do Enem 2025 — Foto: reprodução

A Defensoria Pública do Distrito Federal vai realizar, nesta quinta-feira (5) , a 9ª edição do Aulão Preparatório para a redação do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) . O evento acontece no auditório da Câmara Legislativa do DF, das 14h às 18h, e tem ingressos limitados .

Além da aula de escrita e forma de redação do exame, o evento vai abordar análises de possíveis temas da redação nos eixos de relevância social, meio ambiente, economia, saúde, cidadania e tecnologia.

🔎 As provas do Enem 2026 acontecem nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro .

Na edição de 2025, o evento atingiu cerca de 700 estudantes do Distrito Federal e chegou a capacidade máxima do auditório. A atividade gratuita será realizada por especialistas, educadores, integrantes da defensoria e conduzidas pela professora Sharlene Leite.

“Uma boa redação nasce de repertório, e repertório se constrói com acesso. Reunir estudantes na Casa do Povo, ao lado da Defensoria e de tantos parceiros, mostra que a união entre instituições transforma preparação em oportunidade”, ressalta a educadora.

articles.title: Melbourne Cup: King's former horse Point Of Law wins prestigious Australian race
articles.summary: Point of Law ridden by Ethan Brown has won Australia's "race that stops a nation".
articles.body:
Australian jockey Ethan Brown has ridden Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles, to victory in this year's Melbourne Cup, the country's most prestigious race.

Point of Law, which was bought from the King earlier this year for an undisclosed sum, was considered an early favourite.

Brown pushed Point of Law from the middle of the pack to take the lead with just a few hundred metres to go.

The Melbourne Cup has run in Australia since 1861 and is often referred to as the "race that stops a nation". With a prize of A$10.2m ($7.04m; £5.3m), it is the country's third richest race, but is considered the most prestigious.

"Don't wake me up, this is every jockey's dream," Brown said in a post-race interview.

Brown said he was telling himself "just stay cool, stay patient" as Royal Supremacy raced more than a dozen lengths ahead, before pushing Point of Law from the middle of the pack to overtake on the home stretch.

The King sold Point of Law to a group of investors including former AFL player Chris Judd and his wife Bec.

Trained by Ciaron Maher, the three-year-old thoroughbred won the Geelong Cup last month.

"He's going to be a superstar horse. He's something special," said Brown. "He's in the best of hands with Ciaron Maher."

Maher had a record seven horses in this year's cup, including the second and third place runners, Zahrann and Juja Kibo.

Brown, who grew up in Alice Springs, said he never dreamed as a kid that he would be riding the Melbourne Cup, but he had been given "a lot of great support" in his career.

Brown said he was "inches from losing my life" after a fall from his horse in a 2023 race sent him to hospital and kept him out of racing for six months.

Tens of thousands of people enjoyed sunny weather at Flemington on Tuesday, where they were also entertained by Robbie Williams. Organisers said the UK pop star's appearance, which included a 10-piece band, backup dancers and pyrotechnics, was the biggest pre-cup performance ever staged at Flemington.

The day was not without controversy. One horse, Asterix, was scratched from the race earlier on Tuesday, after it was discovered a stable worker had administered it the medication penetrene earlier that morning.

The medication is used to treat inflammation and muscle soreness, but no treatments of any kind are permitted on race day. Race stewards said the medication was applied in error but still constituted a "serious breach", the Age reported. Trainer Chris Waller was reportedly fined A$50,000 (£26,000; $35,000) for what he described as a simple mistake by a staff member under pressure.

Outside Flemington, crowds from the Australia-wide "Nup to the Cup" movement also gathered to protest against horse racing on the industry's most high profile day. Some held signs with slogans including "horse racing kills", "don't bet on cruelty" and "no more whips".

Interest in the race among Australians has been declining, according to a Guardian Essential poll, which this year found just 9% of people said they had high interest in the race, and 23% had moderate interest. However more than 60% said it was a unique part of Australia's national identity.

Last year the Melbourne Cup drew a record $382.5 million in bets.

articles.title: La sorprendente confesión de Marc Márquez sobre su nuevo pilotaje
articles.standfirst: Desvela la metamorfosis en su estilo tras su última operación en el brazo derecho
articles.summary: Desvela la metamorfosis en su estilo tras su última operación en el brazo derecho
articles.body: "Me he convertido en Álex, preguntádselo”, soltaba Marc Márquez en DAZN después de su victoria en la carrera dominical del Gran Premio de Malasia de MotoGP, en Sepang. Su hermano no lo aclaró del todo, pero, luego, el del Ducati oficial sí lo hizo. Se trata de algo sorprendente y que choca con lo que ha sido el ilerdense durante toda su trayectoria deportiva: un piloto ‘de izquierdas’. “Diría que fue más una adaptación que una rehabilitación. Simplemente intenté adaptar mi estilo de pilotaje. Piloto de una forma distinta a la del año pasado, pero sigo siendo capaz de ir rápido. Es curioso, pero me va peor en las curvas a izquierdas y mejor en las curvas a derechas”, soltaba. Toda una revelación, pues el de Cervera ha dominado con mano de hierro trazados en los que hay más ángulos a izquierdas que a derechas, como evidenció el pleno de puntos en Sachsenring, por ejemplo, uno de sus talismanes. Pero Sepang tiene diez virajes a derechas y cinco a izquierdas, razón, en parte por la que no vencía desde 2018. “Álex puede confirmarlo viendo los datos. No sé por qué, pero en las curvas a izquierdas no tengo el mismo control, mientras que en las curvas a derechas me va mejor”, recalcó. Todo ha venido a raíz de su última operación en el hombro derecho, la realizada después de su caída en el Gran Premio de Francia, en Le Mans, en mayo, cuando ya habían detectado que un nervio interfería en la articulación y provocaba actos no deseados. Con todo, el leridano soltaba algo igualmente extraño. “Pero, aún y así, es cierto que sigo rindiendo mejor en las curvas a izquierdas que en las de derechas”, reconoció. El nueve veces campeón del mundo alude a otros factores a añadir a este nuevo pilotaje, igualmente condicionados por su situación física. “Ahora mismo, no puedo ser impulsivo, no puedo ser tan explosivo. Si quiero luchar por este Mundial hasta el final, tengo que ser más tranquilo y calculador... pero siempre guiándome por mis instintos. En la segunda mitad de la temporada, logré controlar mis instintos, que siempre han sido un punto débil en mi carrera”, admitió. Marc siempre ha tenido fe en su montura. Cuando muchos, incluso en su propia marca, afirmaban que la actual Aprilia, la RS-GP26 era mejor que su Desmosedici GP26, él lo cuestionó y se reafirmó en Malasia sobre qué ha marcado la diferencia. “El equipo. Ya lo dije, no sé si al principio de la temporada. Tengo la mejor moto y el mejor equipo para lograr lo mejor, y por eso tengo confianza”, reiteró. Otro detalle de su pilotaje resulta clave para comprender por qué el triunfador en Sepang fue capaz de mantener un ritmo bestial, el que le hizo cruzar la meta con 4.172 segundos de ventaja respecto a Pedro Acosta. El mayor de los Márquez usa poco el dispositivo para bajar la altura de su moto, algo que se prohibirá en 2027. Con eso consigue gastar menos sus neumáticos y que pueda apretar al final. Él mismo lo confesó. “Sí, si vas liderando, lo puedes hacer”, soltó. Y Marc lideró desde la primera curva hasta la meta.

articles.title: Valentino Rossi: "Antonelli me recuerda a mí, puede ser uno de los mejores de la historia"
articles.standfirst: Amigos desde hace años
articles.summary: Amigos desde hace años
articles.body: Dentro del aluvión de felicitaciones que Kimi Antonelli recibió después de proclamarse campeón del mundo de F1 en el Gran Premio de México de 2026, hay una que le hizo especial ilusión, la de Valentino Rossi, uno de sus ídolos de toda la vida. El Doctor conoce al joven talento desde hace muchos años. Ya sabía quién era su padre, Marco, y, tras decidirse Kimi por probar suerte en el automovilismo, el boloñés encontró en el de Tavullia un aliado. Ocasionalmente se entrenan juntos en karts cuando sus agendas se lo permiten y el de Mercedes ha acudido en varias ocasiones al Ranch que tiene Vale en su pueblo. Allí casi se convierte en uno más de la Academia VR46; tanto que forjó una gran amistad con Marco Bezzecchi, que fue a verle a Monza este año, por ejemplo, además de buena relación con Pecco Bagnaia, Luca Marini, Franco Morbidelli y otros. Las puertas siempre están abiertas para él. Antonelli nunca ha olvidado la ayuda de Valentino, sus consejos y lo que supone para él, como referente. Así, en el pasado Gran Premio de Italia de F1, en Monza, el transalpino portó un casco especial en el que rendía homenaje al nueve veces campeón del mundo de motociclismo. Rossi admite que se emocionó. "Kimi me conmovió profundamente. Fue genial y fue un placer seguirlo. Verlo convertirse en campeón en su segundo año es una gran satisfacción. En 2026 daba mucho miedo: esperaba que pudiera pelear, pero la progresión que ha tenido con respecto al año pasado ha sido impresionante", exponía en Sky Italia cuando intervino tras la cita mexicana en directo. El '46' destacaba que no ha sido sólo por su monoplaza. "Mercedes ha sido rápido, pero no tan dominante como en el pasado, así que gran parte de este campeonato les pertenece”, proclamaba. Valentino sabe lo que se le viene encima a su compatriota, pues lo vivió. "Se convertirá en un héroe. Y con razón: es un título histórico, porque soy un gran aficionado al automovilismo y siempre he lamentado la falta de pilotos italianos capaces de ganar carreras y campeonatos mundiales. Siempre me pregunté por qué éramos tantos en el motociclismo y todos éramos tan fuertes, pero no en la Fórmula 1. Y debo decir que ahora será difícil para Kimi, porque se convertirá en una superestrella mundial: tendrá que gestionar este aspecto, pero si se mantiene así, no será un gran problema", advirtió. El mito de las dos ruedas recordó sus primeros contactos con Antonelli. "Empecé a oír hablar de Kimi en Migliaro, en karting, donde batió un récord de pista. Así que empecé a seguirlo, y marcó la diferencia desde el principio. Tuvo la suerte de crecer bajo la tutela de Toto Wolff, pero, a juzgar por sus actuaciones este año, les ha recompensado con creces", soltó con ironía. Rossi hasta se atrevió a hacer un pronóstico sobre dónde llegará el competidor de 20 años. "En mi opinión, Kimi puede convertirse en uno de los mejores pilotos de la historia. Puede ganar cuatro, cinco o seis campeonatos del mundo si tiene el coche adecuado. Me recuerda un poco a mí mismo cuando tenía 20 o 21 años, así que disfruto mucho viéndolo correr y animándolo”, concluyó.

articles.title: George Russell must find 'overdrive' in 2027 or it's 'game over' after seeing Kimi Antonelli become F1 world champion, says Martin Brundle
articles.summary: George Russell would have been "broken" to see his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli become world champion, according to Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Antonelli clinched the drivers' title with four rounds to spare on Sunday, becoming the youngest-ever F1 World Champion. Meanwhile, Russell endured another frustrating race, suffering a battery issue on the opening lap before later receiving a 10-second penalty for a collision with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. He eventually finished sixth.

Russell started the season as the championship favourite after comfortably getting the better of Antonelli in 2025. However, he has managed just three wins compared with his team-mate's nine and has generally been outpaced, although he has arguably suffered more than his fair share of misfortune along the way.

"Russell will be broken, because he waited at Williams a long time as a Mercedes junior to get his chance. He got it just as they stopped winning," Brundle told Sky Sports News .

"They suddenly turned up with these new 2026 cars, an early dominant car, it's not dominant right now, but it was certainly in the first phase of the season. And then this kid turns up and just transforms from a bit of a liability in year one to a generational talent in year two.

"George has had to observe that, and I think it's affected his own performance. He's been so unlucky but then Antonelli had his fair share of unreliability, dropping out of races too. What will hit George hardest is that he couldn't match Antonelli for speed, for consistent speed. That's all that matters in this business, the stopwatch, it's a very antiquated system.

"Despite spending hundreds of millions of dollars a year running through F1 cars, we live and die by the stopwatch. George has not been as fast as Kimi, especially in the second half of stints in a run on set of tyres. That's what will get to George.

"It might break George, but I think it'll make him, he'll find an overdrive, he has to. He has to come back next year and lift his game up. Meanwhile, he's had to suffer an awful season for himself. A brilliant season for a 19-year-old who has turned 20 through that season."

Mercedes excused Russell from carrying out his post-Mexico City Grand Prix media duties because the British driver was "distraught" according to team principal Toto Wolff.

The FIA fined Mercedes €5,000 (£4,173) for their driver's absence from his media duties and Brundle says he "doesn't blame" Russell, who posted on social media on Monday , for his reaction.

"We get more access to F1 drivers than any other sport can dream of with top players, or what have you in their sports. I think it was a step too far for George to go and have to congratulate him [Antonelli]," he said.

"He did congratulate him of course, underneath the podium, but to have to put up with questions like: 'How do you feel George? And is this the end of the road for you?' I don't blame him.

"The team got fined and I'd be very happy to pay that. Not to have to basically face the music to the world when I'm at my lowest ebb and I think that's fair enough frankly. George has either got an overdrive or it's game over."

Brundle: Antonelli has all the hallmarks of a multiple F1 world champion

Antonelli has been part of Mercedes' driver programme since he was 12 years old and the team have carefully managed his career after a huge amount of excitement grew when he was winning championships in karting and junior single-seater categories.

Brundle admits he thought Antonelli may "fall apart" at times this season but was impressed to see him "flourish" instead with impressive victories in Monaco, Monza and Austin.

"Being a world champion is a whole new level of pressure on his shoulders, from his country, from going around the world as he will do," he said.

"If he can manage that and have the right people around him to take some of that pressure and expectation away from him and make life a bit easier with getting around the world, he should have the staying power.

"He's young, and he's fit. They don't get smashed up as much in F1 cars these days, unless they're super unlucky, actually. So that's a big factor these days. You don't get hit on the head like we used to. You don't get your legs smashed up like we used to.

"I do think Antonelli has all the hallmarks of a multiple F1 champion. But we'll see, it's really hard to do, as Lando Norris has found this year, to keep the mental and physical aspects of that going into two, three or even four seasons."

Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the final leg of the triple header with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW .

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: A nightmare rookie season, replacing Lewis Hamilton, and the making of F1's youngest-ever World Champion
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes protege, has done it.
articles.body: Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes protege, has done it. The Italian has become Formula 1's youngest-ever World Champion, breaking the record held by Sebastian Vettel, who was crowned champion in 2010 at the age of 23. Antonelli has achieved the feat in just his second season with Mercedes, having endured a difficult rookie campaign before dominating the 2026 season.Nine wins, 16 podiums in 19 rounds and six consecutive victories. His 2026 campaign was a remarkable turnaround from a debut season in which the pressure of replacing a seven-time world champion often showed.Antonelli's Formula 1 journey took a significant turn in August 2024 when Mercedes announced him as Hamilton's replacement for the 2025 season.Hamilton's decision to leave Mercedes for Ferrari brought an end to a hugely successful partnership that had produced six Drivers' Championships and multiple Constructors' titles. Replacing a driver of his stature was never going to be an easy assignment, particularly for an 18-year-old making his Formula 1 debut.However, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff placed his faith in Antonelli, who had impressed through the junior categories.It was not a decision taken lightly. Mercedes were handing one of the biggest seats in Formula 1 to an 18-year-old, with the added responsibility of replacing a seven-time world champion. Antonelli had won the Italian and ADAC Formula 4 championships in 2022 before claiming the Formula Regional European Championship in 2023. He subsequently moved directly into Formula 2, skipping Formula 3 altogether.A difficult rookie season: When expectations became overwhelmingAt the start of his F1 career in 2025, Antonelli secured fourth and sixth positions in China and Japan, showing that the Mercedes protege could compete with the established names on the grid. But the Italian endured a difficult European stretch, with retirements at Imola, Spain, Austria and Britain, alongside disappointing results in Monaco and Belgium.Antonelli later admitted that he had allowed the expectations surrounding him to affect his performances."I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period," he reflected while discussing his difficult rookie campaign.There were encouraging moments, too. Antonelli secured his maiden Formula 1 podium with a third-place finish in Canada. He later finished second in Brazil and added another podium in Las Vegas. He ended his debut campaign with 150 points and three podium finishes, despite the difficult spells through the season.The 2026 turnaround: From rookie to championThe first season had given Antonelli a difficult introduction to Formula 1. He returned in 2026 with a better understanding of the demands of the sport and the expectations that came with driving for Mercedes.He finished second at the Australian Grand Prix before producing a breakthrough performance in China. After securing his maiden Formula 1 pole position in Shanghai, Antonelli converted it into his first Grand Prix victory.The Italian briefly lost the lead to Hamilton at the start but recovered his position before the end of the second lap. He subsequently controlled the race and crossed the finish line 5.5 seconds ahead of teammate George Russell.At 19, Antonelli became the second-youngest Grand Prix winner in Formula 1 history and the first Italian to win a race in the sport since Giancarlo Fisichella in 2006.He followed that performance with another victory in Japan, establishing himself as a serious championship contender.Nine victories that defined Antonelli's championship seasonAntonelli's 2026 campaign was built around nine Grand Prix victories. His maiden win in China was followed by another victory in Japan. He continued his run with victories in Miami and Canada before adding Monaco to his growing list of achievements.He also won in Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United States, taking his season tally to nine Grand Prix victories.His victory in Mexico was among the standout performances of the campaign. The middle portion of the season, however, was not without setbacks. Antonelli retired in Barcelona and finished 15th at the British Grand Prix.How Antonelli dominated the championship standingsAfter victories in China and Japan, Antonelli moved to the top of the World Championship standings. Even when wins proved difficult to secure, he continued to collect valuable points through podium finishes and top-five results.By the end of the Mexico City Grand Prix, Antonelli has 380 points, giving him a 119-point advantage over his closest challenger, Max Verstappen, who had 261 points.Lewis Hamilton is third in the standings with 259 points, followed by George Russell on 250.Antonelli's championship-winning campaign included nine Grand Prix victories, 16 podiums, seven pole positions and seven fastest laps.Mexico City: The race that crowned Antonelli championAntonelli arrived at the Mexico City Grand Prix knowing that a ninth-place finish would be enough to secure the championship, regardless of his rivals' results.Starting fifth on the grid, the Mercedes driver faced a race interrupted by a red flag following an accident involving Valtteri Bottas. A late Safety Car period after Arvid Lindblad's crash added further uncertainty.Verstappen eventually secured the victory, with Hamilton finishing second. Antonelli, however, held on to third place and brought his Mercedes home.The 15 points he collected were enough to put the championship beyond mathematical reach.When his race engineer Peter Bonnington confirmed the title over team radio, Antonelli could barely contain his emotions."We did it! Thank you so much," he responded.Breaking Sebastian Vettel's recordAntonelli's championship also brought an end to Sebastian Vettel's long-standing record as Formula 1's youngest-ever World Champion.Vettel had won his first Drivers' Championship with Red Bull in 2010 at the age of 23 years and 134 days. Antonelli surpassed that mark at 20 years and 68 days, becoming the youngest driver in the sport's history to win the title.He also became Italy's first Formula 1 World Champion since Alberto Ascari, who secured back-to-back titles in 1952 and 1953.The difference between his first and second seasons was evident in the results. From 150 points and three podiums in 2025, Antonelli progressed to 380 points, nine victories and 16 podiums in 2026.Hamilton's departure opened the door, and Wolff's faith gave him the opportunity. Antonelli has now delivered the championship Mercedes backed him to win.KIMI ANTONELLI IS THE 2026 FORMULA 1 WORLD CHAMPION.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sergi Ávila, el preparador de Antonelli: "Bajó a buscarme a la calle y nos abrazamos y no le conocía de nada"
articles.standfirst: El fisio barcelonés, de 36 años, desvelaba el lado más personal del campeón, en DAZN F1.
articles.summary: El fisio barcelonés, de 36 años, desvelaba el lado más personal del campeón, en DAZN F1.
articles.body: Sergi Àvila (Barcelona, 1994), es uno de los hombres clave en la carrera de Kimi Antonelli, como fisio personal y preparador físico. Lo conoció en 2022, a través de Aleix Casanovas, el preparador de su compañero George Russell. Ambos se licenciaron en Ciencias del Deporte por la Universidad de Barcelona y posteriormente fueron a Finlandia. Cuando fue llamado para hacerse cargo de Kimi, en 2022, el astro italiano tenía 16 años, estaba en la F4 y el entrenador catalán lo dejó todo para tratar una muñeca recién operada que le daba problemas. La función de Sergi va más allá de la preparación física: coordina el entrenamiento (fuerza, cuello, cardio, natación), la nutrición, los aspectos médicos y psicológicos, el control del sueño, la gestión del estrés, los planes para el desfase horario, la planificación del equipo y los asuntos de marketing y comunicación. Àvila apoya al piloto italiano tanto en la pista como en su vida diaria, con una relación que va más allá del ámbito puramente deportivo. Tras la consecución del campeonato del mundo en México por parte de Antonelli, Sergi concedía una entrevista a Diego Campoy (DAZN F1) delante del box de Mercedes y hablaba sobre los aspectos personales y la forma de trabajar del campeón de F1 más joven de la historia. Pero sobre todo, arrojaba luz sobre su personalidad y la forma en la que relaciona con sus más cercanos. "¿Tú te acuerdas el día que le conociste?", le preguntaba el periodista español. "Me acuerdo muy bien, sí, sí. Fue en 2022, yo dejé Finlandia y fui a Bolonia rápido, porque además a él le habían operado la muñeca, y me acuerdo que fui del aeropuerto directo a su casa, y él bajó y me vino a buscar y nos abrazamos... Nunca habíamos visto antes, y de ahí ya me di cuenta que era un chico especial como persona, de valores humanos increíbles, humilde, un chaval normal, y como he dicho siempre. Es un gustazo trabajar con él, estoy muy feliz de compartir el día a día con un deportista así, porque hay veces que, bueno, las relaciones pueden ser un poco más difíciles, pero en este caso es muy fácil, fluye todo, así que estoy muy contento", relataba "Sí, es una persona con una gran inteligencia emocional, muy sensible. Muy de su gente cercana, un trato humano muy cercano, lo veis también con los mecánicos, la primera cosa siempre que hace, aunque vayamos tarde, que a mí me pone nervioso, que vas tarde al meeting, no, no, no, viene, está en trato con los mecánicos, eso es una de sus cualidades y grandes virtudes. Siempre se hace con el garaje, con el box, porque su sitio más feliz es estar aquí, entonces es muy natural y todo fluye para él, su hábitat natural es estar aquí y por eso contagia una energía muy positiva y muy buenas vibras y entonces eso ayuda al resto a hacer aún mejor el trabajo de todos, eso es una gran calidad suya". "Es increíble, es una cosa que trabajamos mucho desde el principio y de los años anteriores también, este año los resultados han venido mejor, pero siempre enfocados en lo que viene, el próximo paso. Siempre con los pies en el suelo, siempre mucho trabajo. También me preguntaba, yo decía, no, no, no celebramos, pensamos en la próxima. Pero hoy sí, hoy sí, hoy sí que toca, hoy toca, hoy nos tenemos que dejar llevar, esto no pasa casi nunca, no sabes cuándo se puede volver a repetir, así que hay que disfrutar del momento", decía tras la carrera. "Ahora empiezo a darme cuenta de lo que hemos conseguido. Sí, súper feliz porque personalmente también he tenido que hacer muchos sacrificios,. Ha habido momentos muy muy duros, aunque fueran normales, que no se saben, y sí, me estoy emocionando un poco ahora, pero sí, al final cuando acepté este trabajo, dejé todo lo que estaba, me mudé a Bolonia por el proyecto. "Yo antes no sabía ni quién era Kimi, no lo conocía nada y es", reconocía. Y habla de su planteamiento personal. "Para mí es un trabajo que tienes que hacer, el alto rendimiento, si quieres conseguir lo máximo y llegar a ser campeón del mundo, tienes que dar absolutamente todo y eso conlleva que hay ciertas cosas que las tienes que dejar aparte, pero es tu decisión, entonces yo estoy muy contento de haber tomado esta decisión. Sé los pros y los contras y la balanza es positiva, entonces sí, súper feliz y muy agradecido, muy agradecido de la oportunidad, la de Kimi, del equipo, el ambiente en Mercedes es increíble, hacen las cosas muy fáciles" , cerraba Sergi Ávila.

articles.title: F1 Q&A: Hamilton and Leclerc tension at Ferrari, Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix, Ocon's future and red flags
articles.summary: BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions after the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest world champion by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishing second.

Hamilton was unhappy with his team-mate Charles Leclerc and said Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in Mexico.

BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions.

McLaren has its 'papaya' rules, is it now time for Ferrari to introduce its 'Maranello' rules? - John

The battle between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap in Mexico, and the fall-out from it, provided a perfect illustration of the problems that can arise when a team has two top drivers of equal status.

Hamilton's point after the race was that Ferrari would have won the race - probably got a one-two - if the pair had worked together on that first lap.

"When your team-mate works against you and then you lose positions like that, it's definitely tough," he said.

Team boss Frederic Vasseur aldo bemoaned the loss of a potential one-two, admitting he was "frustrated".

Leclerc argued that it takes two to tango. "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One," he said, "but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be."

Leclerc added: "At the end we both did a mistake going into Turn Four. It's not like we had contact whatsoever. We both went straight and that gave the opportunity for Max to overtake. So I don't think it should be that much of a talking point."

Clearly there is a problem here. It's not the first time the Ferrari drivers' competing priorities have caused issues this year, and Vasseur has yet to find a way to manage it effectively, and get the drivers to buy into what he decides.

In this case, the two drivers are expressing two completely different, but valid, points of view.

Hamilton is thinking of the team result - which conveniently also meant a win for him - Leclerc primarily about the fact that they are allowed to race for the win.

The problem is that the team's result was compromised and a win thrown away.

Had Verstappen not passed Hamilton as a consequence of the incident, Leclerc could have given the place back by Turn 11 as was required by the rules.

But once Verstappen was between them, continuing in the lead was Leclerc's only realistic option.

This is a really difficult situation for Vasseur to handle.

The team wants to win the race as first priority, but the same applies to each individual driver. Sometimes those two competing priorities clash.

And if Ferrari ever get themselves a car that can compete for the title, it will only get harder, because the stakes for both drivers are then much higher.

McLaren have done better at handling this, and Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been more acquiescent, but even their approach has led them into problems, as happened a number of times last year. And sometimes the drivers ignore it, as with the crash between the two drivers in the sprint in Singapore.

Vasseur's problem is that if he had asked the drivers not to race on the first lap on Sunday, he would have been essentially asking Leclerc to hand Hamilton a win. And how do you keep an ambitious driver happy in that situation?

One also has to ask whether, if the situations were reversed, Hamilton would accept the same request.

Hamilton revealed after the race that Ferrari "don't have rules of engagement, and whether or not that would change anything from Charles' side, I don't know".

McLaren have rules of engagement. One is not to crash into each other. That's not what happened here. Another is that the team result comes first. But it's very hard to come up with specific rules that would deal with a live racing situation such as this.

One could argue all day about the rights and wrongs and who could have done what to engineer a better outcome.

As Hamilton said: "We've just got to figure out. But something needs to change for sure."

Given that Yamaha have withdrawn from MotoGP in Qatar (and, I understand, much of the media aren't going), why is F1 still so intent on going? The US mid-terms are potentially a trigger point. The risk seems too high. - Richard

This weekend's Qatar MotoGP has been a subject of controversy in motorcycle racing in the context of the war in the Middle East.

First, the vast majority of riders wrote a letter to the sport's bosses saying they would prefer not to race there, and at the weekend Yamaha pulled out of the race, citing a company-wide travel policy.

The race is still going ahead. MotoGP, like F1, is owned by US group Liberty Media.

Similar concerns also exist within F1 on a widespread basis about the end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi going ahead.

Privately, many people within the sport have significant misgivings about going to the Middle East, but those opinions are by and large not being voiced publicly.

One person who has done so is Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who said at the US Grand Prix: "(The sport's bosses) seem very convinced that it's going to go ahead.

"On my personal side, and not speaking as the GPDA, it's very difficult to be convinced right now because there are still things happening in the Middle East, and also there is obviously an election that is going to happen in the US and things that are going to happen on the political side of the world that could affect the next month, month and a half, very suddenly.

"So, I think it's relatively premature to be so convinced."

It's hard to argue with the factual basis for those remarks. Nevertheless, Sainz and Williams were subsequently spoken to by F1, after which Williams put out a statement "clarifying" his remarks.

F1's argument is that it has no reason to cancel the races.

The governments in question are said to be insisting there are no significant risks and that there have been no attacks on civilian infrastructure for nearly six months.

The UK government is not advising people not to travel to those countries.

And F1 not only has lucrative race contracts in place, but Qatar and Abu Dhabi are both heavily embedded in the sport. For example, Qatar is a co-owner of the Audi F1 team; Abu Dhabi is a co-owner of McLaren.

And the concern is, if these races are cancelled, not only would F1 lose the money, but when could it go back to the Middle East? The two wars in question - between the US/Israel and Iran and between the Houthi separatists in Yemen and Saudi Arabia - could continue for years.

However, many people in F1, including a number at a very high level, believe holding the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi at the end of the season is the wrong thing to do in the circumstances.

Many senior figures privately consider the "worst-case scenario", as one put it the other day.

Imagine the situation stays quiet, and then the missiles start flying again once the sport is out in the Middle East.

If that means personnel are trapped there and can't get out, never mind people getting hurt or even killed, the PR consequences for F1 would be enormous.

F1 is not deaf to these concerns. But it is caught between a rock and a hard place.

Essentially, it's waiting to see whether the situation escalates in the context of last week's Israeli election result, or the US mid-term elections, which are being held on Tuesday.

That's why Imola is being prepared as a back-up to replace Abu Dhabi if the two races cannot go ahead.

For practical reasons a decision cannot be delayed much longer. Morally, a number of people in F1 are arguing privately that it should already have been made.

But the complexities of the situation mean the sport remains in limbo, and the races are going ahead as a default position.

Given Estaban Ocon's withdrawal from Mexico and an apparent breakdown in the relationship with Haas, what does this mean for the rest of his season? Will Haas drop him for Ryo Hirakawa? - Josh

Esteban Ocon was dropped by Haas for the rest of the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend after what appears to have been some kind of confrontation between the Frenchman and team boss Ayao Komatsu on Friday after practice.

That followed a dispute between Ocon and race engineer Laura Mueller about tyre choices during second practice.

Haas have not said anything about the dispute or what led them to drop Ocon.

Ocon put out a statement admitting that there had been "a difference in viewpoints (that) led to a discussion with the parties involved" but saying he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature".

As of now, there is no further information.

On Saturday, a source said that, at that point, the move was only for that weekend.

But it's possible Ocon has driven his last race for Haas, given whatever happened was obviously serious enough for Komatsu to take such significant action and the Frenchman is due to leave the team at the end of the season anyway.

If that's the case - and it will become clear in the coming days - then Haas have two obvious options.

One is to continue with Hirakawa, who did a creditable job in Mexico. The other is to bring in Rafael Camara, who has already been signed for next year.

Why are cars allowed to change tyres if a red flag is called? This sometimes ruins a tense end to the race. - Ken

Debate about this rule has continued periodically since the 2011 Monaco Grand Prix, when it appeared to end prospects of a grandstand finish between Sebastian Vettel, Fernando Alonso and Jenson Button.

They were running one-two-three with Vettel on the oldest tyres, which may well have not made it to the end, Alonso on newer ones and Button on newer again when there was a crash and a red flag and the tyre jeopardy was removed.

Every time there is a red flag when drivers are on tyres of different life or compound competing for a win, people bring up the way this rule erases any potential for that battle to play out.

But the rule is in place for safety reasons, for example in case anyone has run over debris and damaged their tyres.

There does not seem to be an attitude to address or change it.

Send us your question for F1 correspondent Andrew Benson

articles.title: ¿Qué número llevará Antonelli en 2027?
articles.standfirst: El Campeón del Mundo de F1 2026 explica las razones del número que usará a partir de ahora
articles.summary: El Campeón del Mundo de F1 2026 explica las razones del número que usará a partir de ahora
articles.body: Ser Campeón del Mundo te da una serie de privilegios a lo largo de la temporada que dure tu reinado, inclusive, usar ese número tan especial que tantos anhelan conseguir: el 1. Sin embargo, y a pesar de tener ese honor que tanto cuesta conseguir, son muchos los pilotos que lo rechazan. Ha sido el caso del recientemente coronado Campeón del Mundo de F1, Kimi Antonelli. El Gran Premio de México ha sido, sin lugar a duda, el más especial para el joven Kimi Antonelli. El piloto italiano de apenas 20 años y 68 días consiguió alzarse con la corona de la máxima categoría del automovilismo, tras una temporada, sencillamente espectacular, en la que ha pasado por encima a toda la parrilla. "Parecíamos 'tontos' a su lado, y es un halago", declaró el hasta entonces Campeón del Mundo, Lando Norris. Sin embargo, y a pesar de la gesta que acaba de conseguir, el de Mercedes prefiere seguir con los pies en la tierra. Seguir enfocado en su trabajo y mejorar porque, tal y como dijo su padre, Marco, tras ver a su hijo proclamarse Campeón del Mundo: "Lo fácil ya está hecho. Ahora toca lo difícil... mantenerse". Y así pues, del mismo modo piensa Kimi: "...me ayudará a mantenerme con los pies en la tierra. Mantenerme humilde. Siento que manteniendo el '12' me permitirá tener un nuevo punto de vista desde dónde empezar y construir todo de nuevo. Mejorar". Aun así, Kimi no ha sido el único piloto en mantener su número. De hecho, todo lo contrario, pues ha habido varios que no quisieron renunciar a un dorsal que para ellos significa mucho. Sin ir más lejos, Lewis Hamilton, por ejemplo, tras su primer título con McLaren en 2008, optó llevar el '1' en 2009. Sin embargo, la siguiente temporada la perdió y, cuando volvió a ganar con Mercedes, decidió mantener su dorsal 44. No fue pues hasta 2022 que volvimos a ver el '1', tras ganar Max Verstappen el Campeonato del Mundo a Lewis Hamilton en 2021. El neerlandés apartó por cuatro temporadas consecutivas (2022, 2023, 2024 y 2025) su mítico '33', hasta este 2026, cuyo '1' fue traspasado a Lando Norris, tras ganar en 2025. Sin embargo, Verstappen no regresó al #33 pues, tal y como él mismo explicó, siempre su número era el 3 pero, cuando llegó a la F1, lo tenía Daniel Ricciardo, por lo que optó por el 33. Al perder su reinado en 2025 y no estar el australiano presente en la parrilla de F1, finalmente pudo lucir ese '3' que tanto deseaba. Ahora, tocará ver si Lando Norris regresa a su '4', del cual ha hecho su marca personal, a pesar de haber lucido el #1 durante una temporada entera, o por el contrario decide probar suerte con otro número. Kimi Antonelli comenzó a lucir ese número 12 en honor a su ídolo, Ayrton Senna: "Es un número muy especial para mi". El legado que dejó el brasileño supone mucho para el italiano y haber ganado el Mundial a puertas del Gran Premio de Brasil, hace que su número y su gesta cobre aún más importancia para Kimi. Es por ello que el recientemente proclamado Campeón del Mundo tiene preparado un casco especial para conmemorar, no sólo a Senna, sino el 35 aniversario de su mítica victoria en casa, Interlagos 1991. "Va a ser un casco homenaje a Brasil, a Ayrton, y creo que es uno de los mejores cascos que he hecho. Así que espero que a vosotros, a todo el mundo, os guste. Va a ser un fin de semana muy especial. Lo estoy deseando porque el apoyo de Brasil en general ha sido increíble, no solo este año, sino ya desde el año pasado". Además, Antonelli ha dado razones, no sólo de mantener el '12', sino de rechazar rotundamente el dorsal 1 pues, a lo largo de su corta carrera ha habido tan sólo dos ocasiones en las que Kimi no ha lucido el #12. En 2024, en la F2 se le identificaba con el '4', y en 2020, el '1'. Es ahí dónde está el problema, pues no fue una de sus mejores temporadas. El italiano corría por aquel entonces en el Campeonato del Mundo de Karting cuando en una carrera en mojado en Portimao tuvo un incidente con Maya Weug, quien salió ilesa, aunque Kimi, por el contrario, se fracturó su pierna y pie izquierdo. "Además, siendo honesto, soy muy supersticioso y el 1 nunca ha sido un buen número para mí. Siempre que lo he llevado me ha ido muy mal. Así que, una razón más para quedarme con el '12' ", incluía Kimi en sus motivos.

articles.title: George Russell: "Realmente te mereces el título"
articles.standfirst: El británico aclara sus sentimientos tras haber perdido el Mundial
articles.summary: El británico aclara sus sentimientos tras haber perdido el Mundial
articles.body: La dicha que provoca en los fans de la F1 tener un nuevo Campeón del Mundo no siempre deja ver la otra cara de la moneda. Para que Kimi Antonelli se haya podido alzar con la corona que le proclama rey de la F1, ha tenido que haber 21 perdedores. Sin embargo, hay uno que destaca de forma peculiar y, cuanto menos, dolorosa si se ve desde su punto de vista. Una temporada y un Mundial al alcance de su mano, pues George Russell por fin tenía un coche con el que luchar. Su sueño estaba más cerca que nunca. Sin embargo, le salió un rival de los pies a la cabeza que le plantó cara y le acabó arrebatando eso por lo que tanto había luchado. Es por ello que, tras perder definitivamente su sueño desde que apenas era un crío, Russell quedó completamente devastado. El británico no se quedó a la celebración de Kimi, algo que fue cuanto menos comentado por los fans y la prensa. Sin embargo, todo parece indicar que el piloto de Mercedes ya tenía el vuelo y actos programados en Brasil, por lo que, no hubo tal ofensa a Kimi ni a Mercedes. El problema es que, a veces, tener el mejor arma para luchar no es sinónimo de victoria y es precisamente lo que le ha sucedido a Russell. El británico ha tenido la fortuna de pilotar el mejor coche esta temporada, pero, desgraciadamente, no lo ha podido tener todo, pues ha carecido de buena suerte, esa misma que muchas veces es necesaria. De las 19 carreras disputadas hasta ahora, Russell tan sólo ha ganado 3 carreras y ha subido 8 veces al pódium. Además, a esos números tan pobres se le añaden 4 ceros: 3 por DNF y 1 por estar fuera del TOP10. Todos esos números, sumado a las 9 victorias de Kimi, los 16 pódiums y los 2 ceros, 1 por DNF y otro fuera del TOP10, hacen prácticamente imposible que Russell le pudiera plantar cara. A pesar del dolor que le pueda producir el haber perdido el Mundial de tal forma, George Russell ha lanzado un comunicado a través de sus redes sociales, dejando una profunda reflexión sobre lo que ha sido su temporada. "Ahora parece un buen momento para hablar desde el corazón. Esta temporada empezó tal y cómo esperaba, pero rápidamente se desmoronó con mala suerte. Ha sido la primera temporada de mi carrera, propiamente dicha, dónde ha habido más días malos que buenos. ¿Ha sido difícil de gestionar? Sí, mucho. ¿Ha sido duro recuperarme semana tras semana? Sí, mucho. ¿Confusa por momento? A veces. Todo lo que sé es que he dado todo lo que soy y 2026 no estaba destinado a ser mi año. Quiero sinceramente felicitar a Kimi por su increíble temporada. Realmente te mereces el título. Gracias al equipo por darme el mejor coche y el mejor motor esta temporada; ha sido inspirador ver a todo el mundo unido para devolver a Mercedes a lo más alto tras varios años duros. Ahora, todo lo que puedo prometer es que, para lo que resta de temporada y de cara a la siguiente daré mi absoluto todo para demostrar de nuevo lo que h sido capaz de hacer la mayor parte de mi carrera y con los dedos cruzados para que vuelva un poco de buena suerte", escribía Russell en su Instagram.

articles.title: La apuesta de Toto Wolff es realidad: "Kimi es humilde, no le distrae el ruido, entiende y ejecuta"
articles.standfirst: El CEO de Mercedes F1 habla de las cualidades de Antonelli, que ha cambiado las críticas iniciales por admiración global
articles.summary: El CEO de Mercedes F1 habla de las cualidades de Antonelli, que ha cambiado las críticas iniciales por admiración global
articles.body: Toto Wolff es una de las personas más felices tras el título de Kimi Antonelli. El CEO de Mercedes AMG F1 es quien apostó por él y decidió en 2024 que sería el sustituto de nada menos que Lewis Hamilton. Y detrás se dice que hay una cuestión personal... la de que en 2013 Red Bull se le adelantó para quitarle a Max Verstappen, con la promesa de llevarlo en 2015 desde la F3 a la F1 como piloto oficial de Toro Rosso de forma directa. Tenía esa espinita de querer tener a su joven estrella campeona y cuando se le presentó la ocasión, con la marcha de Hamilton, no lo dudó. Meterle en todo un Mercedes, siete veces campeón del mundo (seis con Hamilton y una con Rosberg) no es lo mismo que tener a un filial. Se trataba de una apuesta arriesgada, por la que se le criticó sin piedad en 2025, pero que ha funcionado mejor de lo que esperaba: campeón del mundo en su segundo año en la élite. "No solo es que sea fuerte en talento, también tiene un gran carácter. Es humilde... Puede compartimentar, no le distrae el ruido... La forma en la que procesa información es sobresaliente. Si le enseñas una serie de datos los entiende y en la siguiente sesión, el problema desaparece y es capaz de ejecutarlo todo", resumía Wolff en DAZN F1. Wolff era incapaz de decidirse por un Mundial de ente todos los ganados, tras la pregunta de Tomás Slafer en DAZN: "Todos fueron muy especiales. Nico ganó el campeonato contra uno de los mejores de toda la historia y se lo merece porque lo dio todo. Sobre Lewis, estoy orgulloso de haber estado en el camino junto a él y es el piloto más culturalmente relevante... Y ahora es el más joven", enumeraba el austriaco. "Le conocemos desde que tenía 11 años y para mí es casi surrealista verlo porque sigue siendo un bebé. Y el bebé es campeón del mundo, no me lo creo", añadía sobre el logro de alguien tan joven, tres años menos, que el anterior detentor del logro, Sebastian Vettel. Toto ha igualado a Frank Williams (16 título entre pilotos y constructores) y sólo Ron Dennis, el histórico jefe de McLaren desde los años 80, tiene ahora más que director de Mercedes. Se negaba a autoproclamarse como el mejor técnico de la historias. "Eso no lo puedo decir. Si miro a Frank o Ron, Frank Williams o Ron Dennis, son propietarios icónicos y yo no me veo en ese club. Quizás algún día cuando termine podremos dibujar una línea y preguntarnos, fue bueno, es lo que esperaba de mí mismo, pero aún no he llegado", subrayaba. Hablaba luego de su reacción y de cómo vivió el logro de Antonelli. "Es bastante interesante porque durante la carrera estaba ahí sentado y no tenía nada de emoción, incluso pensaba... esto es extraño", reconocía. "Estaba en mi modus operandi durante la carrera porque lo he hecho tan a menudo y ya cuando lo he visto, entonces ya ha sido muy emotivo. Ahora tengo la duda. También soy padre de familia y probablemente me iré a casa... Pensé en quedarme a la celebración, pero prefiero volver (a Europa) y estar con mi familia", decía sobre si quedarse o no a la celebración antes de viajar a Brasil, donde acabará este intenso triplete.

articles.title: Liam Lawson admits 'no assurance' given to him of retaining Racing Bulls seat for 2027 Formula 1 season
articles.summary: Despite his strong performances at Racing Bulls this year, Liam Lawson's future appears to be up in the air as Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov has emerged as a threat to his seat; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo GP at 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Lawson is the highest-placed midfield driver in the F1 Drivers' Championship, with only the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers ahead of him in the standings.

The 24-year-old has scored more than twice as many points as team-mate and rookie Arvid Lindblad and underlined his strong campaign by finishing seventh in Mexico after starting from the pit lane.

Racing Bulls are the only F1 team that has not yet officially confirmed either of its 2027 drivers and it is understood Lawson's seat is under threat from Red Bull junior and Formula 2 title protagonist Nikola Tsolov.

"I'm trying my best. Every weekend I'm trying to maximise," Lawson timidly told Sky Sports F1 .

"In Mexico I gave it everything. There's definitely no assurance at the moment [for next year]. It's a tough sport. Right now, I don't know what else to say, really."

Bulgarian driver Tsolov is highly rated by Red Bull as he's competing for the Formula 2 title in his rookie campaign, having been runner-up in Formula 3 last year.

The 19-year-old made his F1 practice debut in Mexico and was only one tenth behind Lindblad, which impressed Racing Bulls chief executive Peter Bayer.

"Honestly, [Tsolov's] performance on Friday was superb. It was his first time in the car, and he integrated into the team absolutely perfectly," Bayer told Austrian outlet ORF .

"Regarding the driver decision, he put in a fantastic performance. That decision rests with [team principal] Alan [Permane], and he will make it, or rather, announce it when he feels the time is right."

Asked whether Lawson has done everything he can to prove himself, Bayer said: "That's the general consensus in the paddock.

"At the same time, our role, as the leading developer of talent in Formula 1, is to continuously bring new drivers through. We've brought 22 drivers into Formula 1, including the likes of Sebastian Vettel, Max Verstappen and others.

"That's why I say that, at the end of the day, the decision lies with Alan. And he will make the right choice for the team. We chatted about that briefly on Saturday."

What else is left to play out in the F1 driver market for 2027?

Despite signing a multi-year contract which began at the start of this year, Valtteri Bottas' future at Cadillac is up in the air.

Cadillac are keen for Formula 2 driver Colton Herta to qualify for a super licence, which would make him eligible to become a full-time Formula 1 driver.

The team have ran Herta in five practice sessions this season to try to gain super licence points, and the American is now just one point away from earning the licence.

Cadillac are set to run Herta again in first practice this Friday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, where, if he drives 100km, he will pick up another super licence point.

"It is important (for Cadillac to have an American driver). It's an American team, it races under an American flag," said Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski.

"I think you've seen in Austin that we're building a strong American identity as well. It's great to have an American driver, it increases the hype.

"But it's also a question of timing. The right driver, when the team is ready for it, and so we're assessing this."

Last month, Haas announced Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will replace Esteban Ocon next year but did not confirm Oliver Bearman's seat.

Both Bearman and Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season.

"There are a few things in the background that we're working on, but it's been very clear that continuing with Haas will be my target, and we're just finalising a few things on that front," said Bearman.

Asked about the delay, Bearman insisted that a deal would have been finalised by this point if it was up to him.

"It's not really in my hands, I can tell you that. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago," he added.

"But there are a few bigger-picture things that we're working on."

Komatsu furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary.

"I have no idea where that comes from," he said.

"I've experienced this sometimes this season as well. People say there's no smoke without fire but really some people will invent a story.

"What happened in Miami? Apparently, I had an argument with (Bearman's team-mate) Esteban Ocon. There's just absolutely zero truth in it and even those people claiming that they had some insider information etc, absolute total nonsense.

"This one again I don't know who smoked up this six-million euros number. The first time I saw it on Instagram, or Stu [Morrison, Haas press officer] forwarded it to me, and I was just like, 'oh another great… somebody has come up and stirred up whatever'.

"I have no comments to make because it's just not even close to the truth. Why do we engage in such an absolute nonsense? What's the point of it?"

articles.title: Álex Márquez, aliviado tras ser intervenido: "Un pasito más para volver a estar al 100%"
articles.standfirst: El bicampeón detalla cómo ha sido su paso por el quirófano en el Hospital Ruber Internacional de Madrid y se fija el GP de Portugal como la ronda para su regreso
articles.summary: El bicampeón detalla cómo ha sido su paso por el quirófano en el Hospital Ruber Internacional de Madrid y se fija el GP de Portugal como la ronda para su regreso
articles.body: Álex Márquez fue uno de los grandes protagonistas del reciente Gran Premio de Malasia de MotoGP. El de Cervera conquistó la pole con un estratosférico crono (1:56.493), pero no pudo plasmar en puntos su posición privilegiada en el Sprint por un error (fruto de la excesiva confianza) que devino en accidente. Luego, en la carrera dominical, se redimió con un valioso tercero (vio ondear la bandera a cuadros después de su hermano Marc y de Pedro Acosta). Total que el bicampeón engordó su cifra de puntos en la general del certamen. Ahora mismo, a falta de tres rondas por disputarse (Qatar, Portimao y Valencia), el ilerdense es octavo con 197 puntos. El mérito añadido del corredor de Gresini es que estaba compitiendo con unos serios problemas en el hombro derecho. Finalmente, el menor de los Márquez ha decidido poner fin a su sufrimiento al pasar por el quirófano en el Hospital Ruber Internacional de Madrid. En dicho centro médico le han intervenido de su lastimado brazo diestro. Y han aprovechado la coyuntura para retirar las placas de su clavícula derecha y los elementos de osteosíntesis de la mano izquierda que le tuvieron que colocar tras el escalofriante percance que protagonizó en la prueba larga correspondiente del Gran Premio de Catalunya cuando se encontró en plena recta con un Acosta con dificultades técnicas en su RC16. El caso es que Álex ha publicado un largo mensaje (acompañado de un par de fotos) en su cuenta oficial de Instagram para explicar cómo ha ido su intervención quirúrgica. "Este lunes fui intervenido en el Hospital Ruber Internacional de Madrid para extraer material de osteosíntesis en mi clavícula derecha y mano izquierda. Además, en el mismo acto quirúrgico, me han realizado una bursectomía artroscópica en el hombro derecho. Para explicarlo de una forma más sencilla, me han retirado las placas y los elementos de fijación que llevaba en la clavícula y en la mano. Además, han eliminado una pequeña bolsa del hombro que ayuda a evitar el roce entre los tendones y la articulación. Esta última intervención se ha realizado mediante artroscopia, una técnica mínimamente invasiva", ha pormenorizado el dos veces campeón mundial. La intención de Álex Márquez es volver a competir en pista con vistas la penúltima cita del curso que se disputa en Portimao (del 20 al 22 de noviembre). Es evidente que no le da tiempo a estar en Qatar, así que el corredor de Gresini pretende volver a la acción cuando ya queden sólo dos grandes premios para caiga el telón de la campaña 2026 del Mundial de motociclismo. En su detallado análisis de su paso por el quirófano deja entrever que es optimista con su futuro inmediato. "La cirugía ha transcurrido sin incidencias y ahora comienza mi recuperación en casa. Quiero dar las gracias especialmente al Dr. Samuel Antuña y a todo el equipo médico por su trabajo. ¡Un pasito más para volver a estar al 100 %! Gracias a todos por vuestro cariño y por estar siempre ahí", ha abrochado el piloto de 30 años.

articles.title: Melbourne Cup: Point Of Law storms to Flemington glory for Ciaron Maher
articles.summary: Ciaron Maher continued his outstanding recent record in major races, training Point Of Law to Lexus Melbourne Cup glory at Flemington on Tuesday; stablemates Zahrann and Juja Kibo filled the places.
articles.body:
Seen as a St Leger hope after finishing fourth in the Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot and winning Newmarket's Bahrain Trophy for former trainers John and Thady Gosden, he was bought privately to continue his career in Australia, winning the Geelong Cup on his first outing for new connections.

With stablemate Royal Supremacy setting a strong pace for the big-race favourite to aim at, the son of Frankel showed a deadly turn of foot to run down the eventual fifth as Maher trained not only the first three home but also the fifth and sixth in the 'race that stops the nation'.

Maher told Australia's Channel Nine : "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but it's got to execute. I certainly didn't know Royal Supremacy was going to lead by that far but there's nothing better than a true staying test.

"Point Of Law has just thrived and I can't thank all the team and the owners enough. What a ride they've been on. It's been a whirlwind really, but I'm very proud of all the team."

Maher, who had previously won the Flemington feature alongside David Eustace with Gold Trip in 2022, also saddled Zahrann to finish the best part of four lengths behind his stablemate in second, with his Juja Kibo claiming the final spot on the podium.

The trainer, who fielded seven runners in total, added: "To get three horses in the first three spots, I'm very proud. It's been a whirlwind really."

Point Of Law was ridden by Ethan Brown who was enjoying his finest hour in the saddle at the venue his career was almost ended in a near-fatal fall in 2023.

Persuaded back to riding by Maher, his precision ride on the 6-1 favourite was the perfect way to repay the trainer, with the jockey saying: "Please don't wake me up. It's an amazing feeling.

"It's been well documented how Ciaron talked me out of horse training at one stage when I was about 22 years old, but he's done nothing but support me and back me.

"I've messed up plenty of times on his horses and he's had nothing but faith. He's believed in me and shown that by putting me on. I'm quite speechless.

"I thought Point Of Law had the best turn of foot in the race by far. He was shuffled back a bit further than I would've liked and I was trying to get him settled, and I looked up and saw Royal Supremacy about 20 in front and thought, 'Oh God'.

"I had to stay cool, stay patient, cut the bend and once he got that clear run in, his turn of foot was enormous. He's going to be a superstar horse, he's something special."

The raiding European party was dominated by Joseph O'Brien's five-strong team, but there was to be no third win in the race for the Irishman with Sons And Lovers achieving the best position, temporarily halting the Maher procession in fourth.

Derby third James J Braddock was next best of the O'Brien contingent in seventh, with George Boughey's Ebor runner-up Hopewell Rock, heavily backed by none other than JP McManus prior to the race, only ninth.

articles.title: Se acabó el 'truco' de Mercedes y Red Bull para 2027
articles.standfirst: La FIA medirá en tiempo (y temperatura) real todas las cámaras de combustión con un sensor
articles.summary: La FIA medirá en tiempo (y temperatura) real todas las cámaras de combustión con un sensor
articles.body: Fue un asunto que quedó aparcado en la pretemporada con un parche de urgencia, el famoso truco en la cámara de combustión de los motores de Mercedes y de Red Bull, con el que lograban alcanzar una relación de compresión de 18:1, en lugar del 16:1 estipulada en el reglamento 2026, que tenían el resto de suministradores. El 28 de febrero de este año, justo después de los test de pretemporada, la FIA ratificó en el Consejo Mundial del Deporte Motor, que Mercedes podía seguir con su motor de entonces en las condiciones en las que está, es decir, con compresión 18:1 frente a la 16:1 que marcaba el reglamento. Se empezaron a medir en frío y caliente (a 130 grados) a partir del 1 de junio (antes del GP de Mónaco), y sólo en caliente, a partir de 2027. Mercedes ya había pasado anteriormente una prueba previa en Brackley, donde sus motores fueron medidos en ese rango, el de los 130 grados, sin que se detectara una diferencia adicional de rendimiento (aunque es probable que sí lo hayan hecho en temperaturas más altas que no había forma de medir en ese momento). Los rivales aceptaron las medidas de forma unánime. La marca de la estrella, que equipa además a McLaren, Williams y Alpine, salí victoriosa con su truco (se dice que de expansión de materiales en el la culata de la cámara en caliente, que reducía el volumen total del cubicaje), en el que hubo diversas opiniones sobre la ganancia final. Para Toto Wolff, CEO de Mercedes eran "un par de caballos, que pueden ser tres", según dijo en Bahréin.... Pero para otros analistas podrían haber llegado a unos 13-15 CV en ciertos circuitos, lo que les podría haber dado una ganancia de entre dos y tres décimas de segundo por vuelta. En aquel Consejo Mundial se dijo que para 2027 habría novedades en las mediciones y eso es lo que va a ocurrir. Según avanza la edición italiana de 'Motorsport.com', el próximo año, el motor Mercedes "ya no contará con la doble cámara de combustión ", ni tampoco con "su sustituto en la culata de Red Bull Powertrains". La relación de compresión se medirá mediante un sensor interior y ya no será necesario "realizar comprobaciones con soluciones alquímicas, después de que se decidiera que la FIA realizaría comprobaciones en caliente con el aceite calentado a 130 grados". Al carecer de las herramientas de diagnóstico para intervenir sin quemarse, "los comisarios federales se vieron obligados a esperar a que la culata examinada se enfriara", antes de proceder con las mediciones. Franco Nugnes explica en la información que, a partir de 2027, con la introducción de un sensor en la cámara de combustión, será posible medir la relación de compresión en tiempo real. ¿De qué se trata? Es la relación matemática entre el volumen máximo y mínimo de la cámara de combustión de un motor de combustión interna. Este valor indica cuántas veces se comprime la mezcla de aire y combustible dentro del cilindro antes de que se produzca la combustión". Con el nuevo sensor la llamada 'doble cámara' desaparecerá, así como el posible truco de materiales que ofrecen una dimensión en frío y otra en caliente, para recuperar la relación estipulada de 16:1 cuando el motor se enfría. Otros elementos como el escape 'soplado' de Ferrari quedarán eliminados, como algunos de los soportes salientes de efecto aero en las alas delanteras o el recorte de la plancha inferior de resina bajo el suelo, que se reduce en 30 cm de longitud. ¿Quiere decirse que el título de Antonelli ha tenido truco? En cierto modo sí, pero no hay que olvidar que se lo ha ganado a Russell y a Verstappen con soluciones parecidas (o la misma) por lo que no se le puede quitar ningún mérito a una temporada perfecta. Tampoco hay que olvidar que McLaren tenía el mismo motor y que sólo ha ganado dos carreras. Los que podrían aducir eso son Ferrari y sus clientes, que quizá sí se vieron perjudicados desde el principio. Los problemas, en el caso de Honda, estaban y están a años luz de eso límites tan críticos y prestacionales, con un motor que estuvo desde el inicio a más de 70 CV de los mejores. Ellos estaban en otra fase de desarrollo, que deben intentar enjugar a lo largo de la próxima temporada.

articles.title: Esteban Ocon will not race for Haas again this season as Rafael Camara replaces him at Sao Paulo Grand Prix
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon will no longer compete for Haas this season; Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will now partner Ollie Bearman at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix
articles.body:
Ferrari Academy driver Camara, who had already been announced to take Ocon's seat from the start of 2027, will become an F1 driver earlier than anticipated.

Frenchman Ocon was dropped midway through the last round in Mexico, with the American team not offering an explanation as to why.

He was subsequently replaced by Ryo Hirakawa from Saturday onwards but the Japanese driver, who was 10th at the Mexico City Grand Prix, is racing in the World Endurance Championship this weekend in Italy.

Hirakawa impressively finished 10th to score a point on his F1 debut on Sunday following post-race penalties for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, plus Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

Haas announced last month that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad, with Brazilian youngster Camara signed as his replacement for 2027.

The Brazilian - current F2 leader - will step in to partner British driver Ollie Bearman at his home race with Ocon confirmed to have been removed for the rest of the season.

A Haas statement read: "TGR Haas F1 team can confirm that Esteban Ocon will no longer compete on its behalf in the 2026 FIA Formula 1 world championship."

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu refused to answer questions on what had happened with Ocon when he was live on Sky Sports on Saturday of the Mexico race.

The Japanese boss says the issue remains an "internal matter".

He said: "Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward.

"The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations.

"Looking ahead, we've chosen Rafael Camara to drive alongside Ollie Bearman at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix."

Haas have not confirmed who will drive at the final three scheduled races in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: Formula 1: Esteban Ocon dropped by Haas after team row
articles.summary: F1 team Haas says Estaban Ocon will "no longer compete on its behalf in the 2026 world championship" after he was dropped for the Mexico Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Esteban Ocon has been permanently dropped by the Haas team.

The Frenchman will be replaced at this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix by Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara, who has been signed by the team for 2027.

Haas released a statement saying Ocon would "no longer compete on its behalf in the 2026 world championship".

The move comes after Ocon was replaced following Friday's practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend, apparently after a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu.

Haas have given no details as to what led them to drop Ocon in Mexico.

Komatsu said in a statement from Haas on Tuesday: "We have now notified Esteban Ocon that he will not return to a race seat with Haas this season.

"Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward.

"The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations."

Ocon, who has driven in 198 grands prix since making his debut in 2016 and has one victory, looks set to be out of a race seat for 2027 as the only teams with potential vacancies - Racing Bulls and Cadillac - are said not to be interested in him.

He is looking for a reserve drive as a way to stay in the conversations in the paddock.

Ocon was dropped on Saturday morning in Mexico City and replaced by Haas' Japanese reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa .

The decision to stand him down came after he had a dispute with race engineer Laura Mueller about tyre choice during second practice on Friday.

The following day, Ocon released a statement saying he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature".

He admitted that "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved".

His statement followed a report in France's L'Equipe which said that a meeting between Komatsu and Ocon "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically".

Haas have not said who will drive in Ocon's place in the remaining races of the season after Sao Paulo this weekend.

articles.title: Colton Herta to run Cadillac FP1 in Brazil as FIA superlicense quest continues
articles.summary: In Brazil, Colton Herta will aim to collect his final FIA superlicense point required to race in Formula 1 following confusion over his points tally
articles.body:
Cadillac test driver Colton Herta will conduct his sixth Friday practice session of the F1 season at this weekend's Sao Paulo GP to collect his missing FIA superlicense point required to race in the series.

Herta, who has been building up for an F1 campaign with private testing, FP1 sessions and a troubled F2 campaign, needs 40 points to obtain the required FIA superlicense. Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results.

Cadillac will now rectify that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car, which yields a single point. Teams are only required to run a rookie in four FP1 sessions per year, but Sao Paulo will be Herta's sixth of the season as the squad is keen for Herta to finally obtain the license.

That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Valtteri Bottas for a second year alongside Perez, or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027.

"I'm really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the MAC-26 for another FP1 session," Herta said. "Interlagos is such an iconic, historic track, and driving an F1 car around there is going to be an awesome experience.

"Every time I've stepped into the car this year, from Barcelona to Budapest, COTA and Mexico City, I've felt more comfortable and better integrated with the engineering team. My goal for Friday morning in Brazil is the same: execute the run plan cleanly, give Checo and the engineers the best possible setup data to start their weekend, and keep building on my progress in the car. I'm grateful to the team for giving me this opportunity."

Cadillac heads to Brazil after a bruising Mexico weekend, which ended with Bottas suffering a high-speed crash in the race due to a sudden front-left suspension failure. Team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team had "implemented mitigations" to avoid a repeat.

"Following our post-race investigations, Valtteri suffered a suspension failure, and we have implemented mitigations going forward," Budkowski said. "I'm also pleased to see Colton return to the MAC-26 for another FP1 outing, stepping in for Checo. His growth in the car across his sessions has been impressive, and his feedback remains invaluable to our 2027 development program."

Herta's bid to obtain his superlicense hit a snag when his car broke down in Monza, leaving the 26-year-old short of the 100km threshold required for the session to award a point. In Brazil, 24 laps of the Interlagos circuit will satisfy that requirement.
